payload.reason: The evidence indicates that the Greenland Ice Sheet (GrIS) melts before the Antarctic Ice Sheet (AIS) during the Last Interglacial (LIG) due to specific climatic conditions and geological processes, which are not merely for modeling convenience.

claims.text: The Greenland Ice Sheet (GrIS) begins to melt before the Antarctic Ice Sheet (AIS) during the Last Interglacial (LIG), contributing to an early peak in sea level.
The melting of the GrIS is driven by continental levering and ocean syphoning, which are significant geological processes affecting ice sheet dynamics.

Understanding the rate and magnitude of ice loss from GrIS and AIS is crucial for estimating the sensitivity of the planet to warmer climatic conditions, indicating that GrIS's earlier melting is linked to climatic changes.
